sentences.text:
The respondent/BBMP, Bengaluru, has made this reference under Sections 76 and 77 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013 (hereinafter referred to as 'RFCTLA Act' for short) for apportionment of compensation amount.

Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: .2. The brief facts of the case is that the land bearing CTS No.602, PID No.63-40-56 measuring 89 Sq. feet of Adugodi village has been acquired for the purpose of widening of Hosuru-Laskar road.
Preliminary notification was issued on 31.12.2011 and final notification has been published in the Gazette on 28.02.2013.
The L.A.O. has passed the award on 18.06.2015.
The L.A.O. has fixed the compensation of Rs.10,12,015/-.

As O.S.No.6730/2013 and O.S.No.26896/2013 were pending for adjudication, the L.A.O. has referred the matter to this Court and has L.A.C. No.38/2017 deposited a sum of Rs.9,10,510/- after deduction of income tax.
The said amount has been kept in FD in the Union Bank of India, Indira Nagar branch, Bengaluru.
.3. After receipt of reference, this court issued notice to claimant and the claimant entered appearance and filed claim statement.

.4. Claimant - Smt. Lakshminarasamma has filed claim statement stating that she is the absolute owner of the acquired property bearing New Municipal No. 56 (CTS-602), PID No. 63-40-45 measuring 89 Sq. feet of Adugodi, Bengaluru.
The claimant claims that she filed a suit in O.S.No.6730/2013 against one V. Padmanabha Naidu for permanent injunction in respect of acquired property.
Similarly the said V. Padmanabha Naidu filed O.S. No.26896/2013 against the claimant in respect of the acquired property.
As such, the LAO has referred the matter to the Court.

Subsequently, the L.A.C. No. 38/2017 claimant and the said V. Padmanabha Naidu amicably settled all their disputes and entered into a memorandum of agreement between them under Section 89 of CPC before the Bengaluru Mediation Centre and hence, claimed that she is entitled to receive the compensation amount in respect of the property acquired in this case.

.5. In order to prove her case, the SPA holder of claimant namely A.M. Suresh is examined as PW.1 and PW.1 filed evidence affidavit, wherein, he has stated in consonance with the claim of claimant and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9.
.6.

On the basis of the above, the point for consideration is that:
"Whether the claimant proves that she is the absolute owner of the acquired property and entitled for the compensation amount deposited to the Court?"
L.A.C. No.38/2017 .7.

Heard the arguments, perused the materials on record, on that basis, my finding on the above point is in the affirmative for the following:
REASONS .8. Point: This is a reference filed under Sections 76 and 77 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 for apportionment of compensation amount.

sentences.text: .9 . The definite case of the claimant in this case is that she is the absolute owner of the acquired property bearing CTS No. 602, PID No.63-40-56 measuring 89 Sq. feet of Adugodi village and the said acquired property has been acquired for the purpose of L.A.C. No. 38/2017 widening of Hosuru-Laskar road.
The L.A.O. has fixed the compensation of Rs.10,12,015/-.
As the suits were pending for adjudication, the L.A.O. has referred the matter to this Court and has deposited a sum of Rs.9,10,510/- after deduction of income tax.
The said amount has been kept in FD in the Union Bank of India, Indira Nagar branch, Bengaluru.
as such, she is entitled for compensation amount.

.10. The case made out by the claimant is that during pendency of the acquisition proceedings, she filed a suit in O.S.No.6730/2013 against V. Padmanabha Naidu in respect of the acquired property for permanent injunction.
Similarly, the said V. Padmanabha Naidu filed O.S. No.26896/2013 against the claimant in respect of the acquired property.

As the suits were pending before the Court,
LAO has referred the matter to the Court.

Subsequently, the claimant and the said V. Padmanabha Naidu settled their L.A.C. No.38/2017 disputes before Bengaluru Mediation Centre and filed compromise petition under Section 89 of CPC, wherein, the said V. Padmanabha Naidu admitted ownership of the claimant and he has consented for receiving the compensation amount by the claimant.
In support of the said claim, the claimant produced the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9.
Of course, Ex.P.1 Special Power of Attorney executed by claimant in favour of her son A.M. Suresh.
Ex.P.2 is certified copy of mediation settlement.
Ex.P.3 is certified copy of of the decree passed in O.S.No.6730/2013.
Ex. P.4
and 5 are certified copies of mediation settlement agreement and decree.
Similarly the claimant produced certified copy of partition deed dated 10.06.2022 at Ex.P.6 along with endorsement issued by BBMP at Ex.P.7.
She has produced tax paid receipt at Ex.P.8 and online certified copy of encumbrance at Ex.P.9.
Ex .P.2 sufficiently discloses that the claimant and V. Padmanabha Naidu entered into a compromise between them.
In the compromise, the said V. Padmanabha Naidu consented for receiving the compensation amount by the claimant.
The said fact is also evident from the compromise decree and petition.
Therefore, in view of the settlement, there is no dispute regarding title of the claimant over the acquired property.
As such, the claimant is only entitled for compensation in this case and the documents produced by the claimant also substantiated her claim.
Accordingly, Accordingly, I answer point No.1 in the affirmative.

In the result following:
ORDER The reference made under Sections 76 and 77 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and L.A.C.
No.38/2017 Resettlement Act, 2013 is hereby allowed.
